examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Separate user/kernel mode transitions from process context switches. A system call or page-fault exception enters the kernel, but the same process may resume without scheduling another. A library call can remain in user space, for example malloc serving an existing allocation. Track which state must be saved before a handler overwrites registers or the program counter.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A process executes 8 ordinary function calls and 3 system calls, with no other exceptions. How many user-to-kernel entries are guaranteed?

**Answer: 3.** Each of the three system calls explicitly invokes kernel service and guarantees an entry. The eight ordinary calls need not enter kernel mode. The guaranteed count is three; scheduler switches need not equal it.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Actual implementations may perform extra system calls inside libraries, but do not assume them when the problem gives only ordinary function calls.

A system call is not guaranteed to transfer all requested bytes in one operation.
